symptomShortText: Exhaust flange weld seam failed helium leak test at customer Tier-1 exhaust plant

defect.defectText: Internal porosity in robotic fiber laser welded lap joint

causesIshikawa.description: EMP-4109, Shift A - robot welding programmer taught seam coordinates per nominal CAD model
EQ-WELD02-001 4kW fiber laser power output 3.2 kW and beam focus BPP verified stable
Shielding gas delivery nozzle bracket bent to 28 deg inclination during robot teaching, creating Venturi turbulent air aspirating into the molten keyhole
Stainless steel AISI 304 flange and tube chemical composition and surface oil-free condition verified
Mass spectrometer helium leak detector GA-0988 calibration certified
Welding booth cross-draft exhaust airflow 0.4 m/s compliant

fiveWhyChain.question: Why did exhaust flange assemblies leak during customer exhaust system leak test?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Helium gas passed through connected subsurface gas pore channels across the laser weld bead

fiveWhyChain.question: Why were continuous gas pores formed in the laser weld keyhole?
fiveWhyChain.answer: Atmospheric oxygen and nitrogen were drawn into the molten pool, generating gas bubbles during rapid solidification
fiveWhyChain.evidenceCitation: Weld metallographic cross-section and gas chromatography

fiveWhyChain.question: Why was the shielding gas envelope compromised during welding? (root cause)
fiveWhyChain.answer: The Argon gas nozzle bracket was deflected to 28 deg after colliding with a fixture clamp during robot touch-up, inducing turbulent air vortexing
fiveWhyChain.evidenceCitation: Robot cell collision log and nozzle geometry inspection

actions.actionText: Sort and 100% helium leak test 92 units at customer plant and quarantine 180 units in transit
Replace flexible nozzle bracket with dowel-located rigid steel mounting block set to 15 deg
Add optical nozzle alignment check to automated daily robot zeroing routine in cell PLC

fmeaLink.description: Laser weld porosity due to shielding gas nozzle misalignment and air turbulence

lessonsLearned.whatWorked: Rigid dowel mounting prevented nozzle bracket angle shift even during tool servicing
lessonsLearned.whatDidnt: Robot minor collision sensor did not force an optical re-alignment check

isIsNot.isWhereWhenItHappens: Exhaust Flange EF-80 welded on WC-WELD-02 robot arm 1 on 2026-08-11
isIsNot.isNotWhereWhenItDoesnt: Flanges welded on WC-WELD-01 with rigid dowel-pinned nozzle bracket
isIsNot.notes: Porosity caused by bent nozzle angle after unrecorded fixture micro-collision
